fields.name: k_population-age|0
fields.title: A.1 Population - Age - Adolescent (13-18 years)
fields.description: Individuals aged 13 to 18 years undergoing puberty and adolescent development, with distinct biological vulnerabilities and behavioural risk profiles compared to younger children and adults.

fields.name: k_population-age|1
fields.title: A.1 Population - Age - Adult
fields.description: Individuals aged 19 years and older, encompassing young adults, middle-aged, and older adult sub-groups across the adult life course.

fields.name: k_population-age|2
fields.title: A.1 Population - Age - All ages
fields.description: Studies or data that encompass individuals across all age groups without restriction, or where findings apply across the full life course.

fields.name: k_population-age|3
fields.title: A.1 Population - Age - Child (2-12 years)
fields.description: Children aged 2 to 12 years, spanning early childhood through to pre-adolescence, during which physical, cognitive, and social development are particularly sensitive to environmental conditions.

fields.name: k_population-age|4
fields.title: A.1 Population - Age - Infant (1-23 months)
fields.description: Children aged 1 to 23 months, a developmental period of rapid growth, nutritional dependency, and heightened susceptibility to infectious disease and environmental exposures.

fields.name: dsny000255_sub|0
fields.title: Adult Category - Adult (19-44 years)
fields.description: Adults aged 19 to 44 years, typically characterised by peak physical capacity, reproductive activity, and workforce participation.

fields.name: dsny000255_sub|1
fields.title: Adult Category - Aged (65 years and older)
fields.description: Individuals aged 65 years and older, a broad group encompassing younger-old and oldest-old adults with increasing prevalence of chronic disease, frailty, and functional decline.

fields.name: dsny000255_sub|2
fields.title: Adult Category - Middle aged (45-64 years)
fields.description: Adults aged 45 to 64 years, a life stage associated with the onset of chronic non-communicable diseases and changing physiological risk profiles.

fields.name: dsny000258_sub|0
fields.title: Aged (65 years and older) Category - Aged (65-78 years)
fields.description: Older adults aged 65 to 78 years, often retaining significant functional capacity but with increasing chronic disease burden and growing vulnerability to environmental stressors.

fields.name: dsny000258_sub|1
fields.title: Aged (65 years and older) Category - Aged (80 years and older)
fields.description: Individuals aged 80 years and older, the fastest-growing demographic in many populations, with the highest prevalence of frailty, multimorbidity, and vulnerability to adverse health events.

fields.name: dsny000251_sub|0
fields.title: Child (2-12 years) Category - Child (6-12 years)
fields.description: Children aged 6 to 12 years in middle childhood, a period of continued physical growth, cognitive development, and increasing social independence.

fields.name: dsny000251_sub|1
fields.title: Child (2-12 years) Category - Preschool child (2-5 years)
fields.description: Children aged 2 to 5 years in the preschool developmental stage, characterised by rapid brain development, high activity levels, and reliance on caregivers for protection from environmental hazards.

fields.name: dsny000249_sub|0
fields.title: Infant (1-23 months) Category - Newborn infant
fields.description: Infants in the first 28 days of life, a critical period of physiological adaptation with high vulnerability to infection, thermal stress, and nutritional insufficiency.

fields.name: k_population-gender-sex|0
fields.title: A.2 Population - Gender/sex - All genders
fields.description: Studies or data that include individuals of all gender identities or both sexes without stratification, or where findings apply across the full gender spectrum.

fields.name: k_population-gender-sex|1
fields.title: A.2 Population - Gender/sex - Diverse
fields.description: Individuals whose gender identity or expression differs from the sex assigned at birth, including transgender, non-binary, and other gender-diverse people.

fields.name: k_population-gender-sex|2
fields.title: A.2 Population - Gender/sex - Female
fields.description: Individuals identified as female by biological sex or gender identity, used to stratify health data or describe sex-specific biological and social health determinants.

fields.name: k_population-gender-sex|3
fields.title: A.2 Population - Gender/sex - Male
fields.description: Individuals identified as male by biological sex or gender identity, used to stratify health data or describe sex-specific biological and social health determinants.

fields.name: k_population-vulnerability|0
fields.title: A.3 Population - Vulnerability - Chronic conditions (Vulnerability)
fields.description: Individuals living with one or more long-term physical health conditions that reduce physiological resilience and increase susceptibility to adverse health outcomes.

fields.name: k_population-vulnerability|1
fields.title: A.3 Population - Vulnerability - Disabled (Vulnerability)
fields.description: Individuals with physical, sensory, cognitive, or mental impairments that limit daily functioning and may increase exposure to harm and reduce capacity to respond to environmental or social stressors.

fields.name: k_population-vulnerability|2
fields.title: A.3 Population - Vulnerability - Ethnic minorities (Vulnerability)
fields.description: Population groups defined by shared ethnic, cultural, or racial identity that may face structural disadvantage, discrimination, or disproportionate exposure to environmental and social risk factors.

fields.name: k_population-vulnerability|3
fields.title: A.3 Population - Vulnerability - Frail elderly (Vulnerability)
fields.description: Older adults with reduced physiological reserve and resilience, characterised by weakness, fatigue, and vulnerability to adverse health outcomes following minor stressors.

fields.name: k_population-vulnerability|4
fields.title: A.3 Population - Vulnerability - Indigenous peoples (Vulnerability)
fields.description: Populations with historical, cultural, and territorial ties to lands prior to colonisation, who often face compounded social, economic, and environmental vulnerabilities.

fields.name: k_population-vulnerability|5
fields.title: A.3 Population - Vulnerability - Infants / children (Vulnerability)
fields.description: Young children and infants whose immature physiological systems, developmental dependency, and limited autonomy increase their susceptibility to environmental exposures and health harms.

fields.name: k_population-vulnerability|6
fields.title: A.3 Population - Vulnerability - Low-income (Vulnerability)
fields.description: Individuals and households with insufficient financial resources to meet basic needs, facing compounded vulnerability through reduced access to healthcare, nutrition, safe housing, and adaptive capacity.

fields.name: k_population-vulnerability|7
fields.title: A.3 Population - Vulnerability - Migrants (Vulnerability)
fields.description: People who have moved within or across borders, voluntarily or under duress, and who may face elevated health risks due to displacement, poor living conditions, and restricted access to services.

fields.name: k_population-vulnerability|8
fields.title: A.3 Population - Vulnerability - Occupation-based (Vulnerability)
fields.description: Individuals whose occupation exposes them to elevated health hazards, including outdoor workers in agriculture, construction, and other sectors with high physical exposure to environmental conditions.

fields.name: k_population-vulnerability|9
fields.title: A.3 Population - Vulnerability - Pregnancy (Vulnerability)
fields.description: Individuals during pregnancy, whose altered physiology and increased metabolic demands heighten susceptibility to environmental exposures and infectious disease with potential consequences for both maternal and foetal health.

fields.name: k_population-vulnerability|10
fields.title: A.3 Population - Vulnerability - Women (Vulnerability)
fields.description: Women as a population group who may face heightened vulnerability due to biological factors, gender-based inequalities in resource access, and higher exposure to specific social and economic risks.

fields.name: k_reference-type|0
fields.title: B. Reference type [automation planned] - Article (academic journal)
fields.description: A peer-reviewed research output published in an academic journal, including full research articles, letters to the editor, commentaries, and opinion pieces.

fields.name: k_reference-type|1
fields.title: B. Reference type [automation planned] - Grey literature
fields.description: Reports published outside the classic editorial route, predominantly by intergovernmental organizations, supra-national organizations, NGOs, governments.

fields.name: k_reference-type|2
fields.title: B. Reference type [automation planned] - Planned research/protocols
fields.description: A registered or published research protocol or trials registry record describing a study that is planned or underway but has not yet reported results.

fields.name: k_reference-type|3
fields.title: B. Reference type [automation planned] - Preprint/working paper
fields.description: A research manuscript that has been made publicly available prior to formal peer review and journal publication, such as those posted on medRxiv or SSRN.

fields.name: k_reference-type|4

fields.name: k_methods|0
fields.title: C. Methods - C.1 Primary research
fields.description: Original research studies that collect and analyse data directly, as distinct from evidence syntheses that aggregate findings from existing studies.

fields.name: k_methods|1
fields.title: C. Methods - C.2 Evidence synthesis
fields.description: Research that systematically or narratively aggregates and synthesises findings from multiple primary studies to draw broader conclusions about a topic.

fields.name: dsny000167_sub|0
fields.title: C.1 Primary research Category - Descriptive / single-group designs
fields.description: Study designs that describe characteristics, frequency, or distribution of outcomes in a single group without a comparison group or temporal manipulation.

fields.name: dsny000167_sub|1
fields.title: C.1 Primary research Category - Experimental / group comparison designs
fields.description: Experimental study designs that compare outcomes between an intervention group and one or more control or comparison groups, with or without randomisation.

fields.name: dsny000167_sub|2
fields.title: C.1 Primary research Category - Experimental / single-group designs
fields.description: Experimental study designs in which an intervention is applied to a single group without a concurrent control group, limiting but not eliminating causal inference.

fields.name: dsny000167_sub|3
fields.title: C.1 Primary research Category - Modelling / simulation
fields.description: Study designs using mathematical, statistical, or computational models to simulate real-world systems, project future outcomes, or estimate impacts under defined scenarios.

fields.name: dsny000167_sub|4
fields.title: C.1 Primary research Category - Observational / group comparison designs
fields.description: Observational study designs that compare health outcomes between two or more groups defined by exposure status, without random allocation.

fields.name: dsny000167_sub|5
fields.title: C.1 Primary research Category - Observational / single-group designs
fields.description: Observational study designs that track outcomes over time in a single group without a concurrent comparison group, relying on temporal patterns to infer associations.

fields.name: dsny000167_sub|6
fields.title: C.1 Primary research Category - Qualitative and mixed-methods designs
fields.description: Study designs using qualitative data collection and analysis, or combining qualitative and quantitative approaches, to explore meanings, experiences, and contextual factors.

fields.name: dsny000167_sub|7
fields.title: C.1 Primary research Category - Z_Other study design
fields.description: Primary research study designs not captured by the specific categories of descriptive, observational, experimental, qualitative, or modelling designs.

fields.name: dsny000515_sub|0
fields.title: Descriptive / single-group designs Category - Case report / case study
fields.description: A detailed account of a single individual's or unit's exposure, condition, and outcome, used to generate hypotheses or describe novel or rare phenomena.

fields.name: dsny000515_sub|1
fields.title: Descriptive / single-group designs Category - Case series / descriptive multi-case study
fields.description: A descriptive report of characteristics and outcomes among a series of individuals sharing a common exposure or condition, without a control group.

fields.name: dsny000515_sub|2
fields.title: Descriptive / single-group designs Category - Cross-sectional / single-round survey
fields.description: A study design that collects data from a population at a single point in time, describing the prevalence of exposures and outcomes without follow-up.

fields.name: dsny000529_sub|0
fields.title: Experimental / group comparison designs Category - Non-randomised
fields.description: An experimental or quasi-experimental study in which participants are allocated to intervention and comparison groups through a process other than randomisation, using statistical methods to control for confounding.

fields.name: dsny000529_sub|1
fields.title: Experimental / group comparison designs Category - Quasi-randomised / natural experiment
fields.description: A study in which allocation to intervention and control conditions occurs through a process that approximates randomisation but is not under the investigator's full control, such as policy roll-out or natural variation.

fields.name: dsny000529_sub|2
fields.title: Experimental / group comparison designs Category - Randomisation unclear
fields.description: An experimental or quasi-experimental study in which the method of allocation to groups is not clearly reported, precluding classification as randomised or non-randomised.

fields.name: dsny000529_sub|3
fields.title: Experimental / group comparison designs Category - Randomised / RCT
fields.description: An experimental study in which participants are randomly allocated to intervention or control groups, considered the gold standard for evaluating causal effects of interventions.

fields.name: dsny000532_sub|0
fields.title: Non-randomised Category - Difference-in-differences
fields.description: A quasi-experimental method comparing the change in outcomes over time between a group exposed to an intervention and an unexposed control group, to estimate causal effects under the parallel trends assumption.

fields.name: dsny000532_sub|1
fields.title: Non-randomised Category - Event study
fields.description: A method estimating the effect of an event or intervention by examining outcome trends relative to the timing of the event, often used to test pre-treatment parallel trends and assess dynamic treatment effects.

fields.name: dsny000532_sub|2
fields.title: Non-randomised Category - Fixed effects / panel regression
fields.description: A regression approach using repeated observations on the same units over time to control for time-invariant unobserved confounding, including standard fixed effects, panel regression, and adjusted cohort analysis.

fields.name: dsny000532_sub|3
fields.title: Non-randomised Category - Instrumental variables
fields.description: A quasi-experimental method using a variable that affects exposure but not the outcome directly (an instrument) to estimate causal effects in the presence of unmeasured confounding.

fields.name: dsny000532_sub|4
fields.title: Non-randomised Category - Matched comparison / propensity score matching
fields.description: A method pairing treated and untreated units on observed characteristics or estimated propensity scores to construct a balanced comparison group and reduce confounding bias.

fields.name: dsny000532_sub|5
fields.title: Non-randomised Category - Regression discontinuity
fields.description: A quasi-experimental design exploiting a threshold in a continuous assignment variable to estimate causal effects for units just above and below the cutoff, where assignment is effectively random.

fields.name: dsny000532_sub|6
fields.title: Non-randomised Category - Synthetic control
fields.description: A quasi-experimental method constructing a weighted combination of untreated units to serve as a counterfactual for a treated unit, used when only a small number of aggregate units are available.

fields.name: dsny000527_sub|0
fields.title: Experimental / single-group designs Category - Single arm trial / single arm experiment
fields.description: An experimental study in which all participants receive the intervention and outcomes are compared to a pre-specified target or historical baseline, without a concurrent control arm.

fields.name: dsny000545_sub|0
fields.title: Modelling / simulation Category - Computable general equilibrium (CGE) model
fields.description: A macroeconomic modelling approach representing interactions across sectors of an economy to estimate the economy-wide effects of policy changes, including those with health implications.

fields.name: dsny000545_sub|1
fields.title: Modelling / simulation Category - Integrated assessment model (IAM) / health impact projection
fields.description: A modelling approach linking climate, economic, and social systems to project future health impacts under different emissions or policy scenarios, often at national or global scale.

fields.name: dsny000545_sub|2
fields.title: Modelling / simulation Category - Microsimulation
fields.description: A modelling approach simulating the behaviour and outcomes of individual units — people, households, or firms — over time to estimate aggregate population-level effects of policies or exposures.

fields.name: dsny000545_sub|3
fields.title: Modelling / simulation Category - Other climate-related modelling / simulation
fields.description: Climate or environmental modelling and simulation approaches not classified under IAM, CGE, or microsimulation, including downscaled climate models, exposure models, and environmental simulation tools.

fields.name: dsny000545_sub|4
fields.title: Modelling / simulation Category - Other health-related modelling / simulation
fields.description: Health modelling and simulation approaches not classified under IAM, CGE, or microsimulation, including epidemiological models, disease transmission models, and burden of disease projections.

fields.name: dsny000522_sub|0
fields.title: Observational / group comparison designs Category - (Controlled) interrupted time series
fields.description: A time series analysis comparing outcome trends before and after an intervention or exposure in both an intervention group and a concurrent control group, strengthening causal inference over uncontrolled ITS.

fields.name: dsny000522_sub|1
fields.title: Observational / group comparison designs Category - Case-control / retrospective matched comparison
fields.description: A study that retrospectively compares individuals with a health outcome (cases) to those without (controls) to identify differences in prior exposure, often using matching to reduce confounding.

fields.name: dsny000522_sub|2
fields.title: Observational / group comparison designs Category - Cohort / panel data / longitudinal study
fields.description: A study that follows a defined group of individuals over time, measuring exposures and outcomes prospectively or retrospectively to assess associations and temporal relationships.

fields.name: dsny000522_sub|3
fields.title: Observational / group comparison designs Category - Controlled before-after (CBA)
fields.description: A study comparing pre- and post-intervention outcomes in both an intervention group and a non-randomised control group, improving on uncontrolled before-after designs by accounting for secular trends.

fields.name: dsny000519_sub|0
fields.title: Observational / single-group designs Category - (Uncontrolled) interrupted time series
fields.description: A time series analysis of outcome data at multiple time points before and after an intervention or exposure in a single group, without a control series to account for concurrent trends.

fields.name: dsny000519_sub|1
fields.title: Observational / single-group designs Category - Before-after / pre-post study
fields.description: A study that compares outcomes measured in the same group before and after an exposure or intervention, without a concurrent control group.

fields.name: dsny000541_sub|0
fields.title: Qualitative and mixed-methods designs Category - Ethnographic / interview-based
fields.description: A qualitative research design using immersive fieldwork, participant observation, or in-depth interviews to explore lived experiences, cultural practices, and social contexts.

fields.name: dsny000541_sub|1
fields.title: Qualitative and mixed-methods designs Category - Focus group
fields.description: A qualitative method collecting data through facilitated group discussion among selected participants, used to explore shared perspectives, norms, and experiences on a defined topic.

fields.name: dsny000541_sub|2
fields.title: Qualitative and mixed-methods designs Category - Mixed-methods
fields.description: A research design that integrates quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis within a single study, combining the strengths of both approaches to address research questions.

fields.name: dsny000198_sub|0
fields.title: C.2 Evidence synthesis Category - Guideline (clinical or public health)
fields.description: A systematically developed statement providing recommendations to guide clinical or public health practice, typically based on a synthesis of the available evidence. Often with systematic methods, but sometimes also based on expert consensus.

fields.name: dsny000198_sub|1
fields.title: C.2 Evidence synthesis Category - Health technology assessment (HTA)
fields.description: A comprehensive policy-relevant evaluation of a health technology that typically includes clinical effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, and broader social and ethical considerations.

fields.name: dsny000198_sub|2
fields.title: C.2 Evidence synthesis Category - Narrative review
fields.description: A non-systematic review that summarises and interprets the literature on a topic based on the author's expertise and judgement, without exhaustive or reproducible search methods.

fields.name: dsny000198_sub|3
fields.title: C.2 Evidence synthesis Category - Systematic review
fields.description: A review that uses explicit, reproducible methods to systematically search, select, appraise, and synthesise evidence from primary studies on a defined research question.

fields.name: dsny000198_sub|4
fields.title: C.2 Evidence synthesis Category - Umbrella review / overview of reviews
fields.description: A synthesis that systematically compiles and summarises findings from multiple systematic reviews on a related topic, providing a high-level overview of the evidence base.

fields.name: dsny000198_sub|5
fields.title: C.2 Evidence synthesis Category - Z_Other evidence synthesis type
fields.description: Evidence synthesis types not captured by the specific categories of systematic review, umbrella review, narrative review, guideline, or health technology assessment.

fields.name: dsny000201_sub|0
fields.title: Systematic review Category - Evidence map / evidence gap map
fields.description: A systematic mapping exercise that visually represents the distribution of evidence across a framework of interventions and outcomes, highlighting areas where evidence is absent or weak.

fields.name: dsny000201_sub|1
fields.title: Systematic review Category - Full systematic review
fields.description: A systematic review conducted with comprehensive search strategies and full methodological rigour, without time or resource constraints that would limit its scope.

fields.name: dsny000201_sub|2
fields.title: Systematic review Category - Mixed-methods review
fields.description: A systematic review that integrates findings from both quantitative and qualitative primary studies, using mixed-methods synthesis approaches to address questions that neither approach could answer alone.

fields.name: dsny000201_sub|3
fields.title: Systematic review Category - Qualitative evidence synthesis
fields.description: A systematic review that searches for, appraises, and synthesises findings from qualitative primary studies, using methods such as meta-ethnography, thematic synthesis, or framework synthesis.

fields.name: dsny000201_sub|4
fields.title: Systematic review Category - Rapid review
fields.description: A systematic review conducted within a shortened timeframe using streamlined methods, trading some comprehensiveness for speed to meet urgent policy or practice needs.

fields.name: dsny000201_sub|5
fields.title: Systematic review Category - Realist review
fields.description: A theory-driven review methodology that explores how and why interventions work in particular contexts and for whom, generating or testing explanatory theories rather than aggregating effect estimates.

fields.name: dsny000201_sub|6
fields.title: Systematic review Category - Scoping review
fields.description: A systematic review that maps the extent, range, and nature of evidence on a broad topic without synthesising findings, used to identify gaps and inform future research priorities.

fields.name: k_topic|0
fields.title: D. Topic - Adaptation
fields.description: Adjustments in natural or human systems in response to actual or anticipated climate change, intended to moderate harm or exploit beneficial opportunities arising from climate variability.

fields.name: k_topic|1
fields.title: D. Topic - Impact
fields.description: The effects of climate change on natural and human systems, including consequences for health, ecosystems, economies, and societies resulting from climate variability and change.

fields.name: k_topic|2
fields.title: D. Topic - Mitigation
fields.description: Actions and strategies aimed at reducing or preventing greenhouse gas emissions in order to limit the magnitude of future climate change and its associated health and environmental impacts.

fields.name: dsny000052_sub|0
fields.title: Adaptation Category - Maladaptation
fields.description: Adaptation actions that inadvertently increase vulnerability or exposure to harm, reduce adaptive capacity, or create new risks for human or natural systems, often as an unintended consequence of well-intentioned interventions.

fields.name: dsny000053_sub|0
fields.title: Impact Category - Attribution
fields.description: The process of establishing the causal contribution of climate change to observed changes in physical, ecological, or human systems, including specific extreme weather events or health outcomes.

fields.name: dsny000053_sub|1
fields.title: Impact Category - Future impact
fields.description: Projected effects on human health, ecosystems, and societies arising from anticipated changes in climate over coming decades, typically derived from climate modelling and scenario analysis.

fields.name: dsny000053_sub|2
fields.title: Impact Category - Loss and damage
fields.description: Negative consequences of climate change that cannot be avoided through mitigation or adaptation, including irreversible harm to lives, livelihoods, cultural heritage, ecosystems, and infrastructure.

fields.name: dsny000051_sub|0
fields.title: Mitigation Category - Co-Benefits
fields.description: Positive health, social, or environmental benefits arising from mitigation actions that are additional to the primary goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions, such as improved air quality or increased physical activity.

fields.name: k_climate-drivers-variability|0
fields.title: E.1 Climate factors - Climate drivers / variability - (Unspecified) changes in weather
fields.description: General changes in weather patterns not attributed to a specific meteorological variable, used when studies refer to weather variability in broad terms.

fields.name: k_climate-drivers-variability|1
fields.title: E.1 Climate factors - Climate drivers / variability - (Unspecified) climate change
fields.description: Climate change where the specific driver or mechanism is not identified or distinguished, used when studies refer to climate change in general terms.

fields.name: k_climate-drivers-variability|2
fields.title: E.1 Climate factors - Climate drivers / variability - Changes in glacier / snow melt
fields.description: Accelerated melting of glaciers and snowpack due to rising temperatures, affecting freshwater supply, sea levels, and downstream ecosystems.

fields.name: k_climate-drivers-variability|3
fields.title: E.1 Climate factors - Climate drivers / variability - Changes in humidity
fields.description: Shifts in atmospheric moisture levels that affect thermal comfort, respiratory health, and the prevalence of moisture-related diseases.

fields.name: k_climate-drivers-variability|4
fields.title: E.1 Climate factors - Climate drivers / variability - Changes in precipitation
fields.description: Alterations in the amount, timing, or intensity of rainfall and snowfall, affecting water availability, flood risk, and drought conditions.

fields.name: k_climate-drivers-variability|5
fields.title: E.1 Climate factors - Climate drivers / variability - Changes in sea level
fields.description: The increase in mean sea level resulting from thermal expansion of seawater and melting ice, threatening coastal communities, infrastructure, and freshwater resources.

fields.name: k_climate-drivers-variability|6
fields.title: E.1 Climate factors - Climate drivers / variability - Changes in season length
fields.description: Shifts in the duration of seasons, including earlier spring onset and extended summers, with consequences for agriculture, vector biology, and human health.

fields.name: k_climate-drivers-variability|7
fields.title: E.1 Climate factors - Climate drivers / variability - Changes in temperature
fields.description: Long-term shifts in average or extreme temperature conditions, including warming trends, that affect human health, ecosystems, and society.

fields.name: k_climate-drivers-variability|8
fields.title: E.1 Climate factors - Climate drivers / variability - Changes in wind speed
fields.description: Alterations in wind patterns and velocity that can affect air quality, energy systems, and the spread of airborne pathogens and pollutants.

fields.name: k_climate-drivers-variability|9
fields.title: E.1 Climate factors - Climate drivers / variability - Climate variability
fields.description: Climate variability refers to fluctuations in climate conditions (temperature, precipitation, wind patterns, etc.) over months, years, or decades around a longer-term average. Climate variability is influenced by multiple climate drivers.

fields.name: k_extreme-weather-events|0
fields.title: E.2 Climate factors - Extreme weather events - (Unspecified) extreme weather events
fields.description: Extreme weather events where the specific type is not identified, used when studies refer to climate extremes without distinguishing between event types.

fields.name: k_extreme-weather-events|1
fields.title: E.2 Climate factors - Extreme weather events - Droughts
fields.description: Prolonged periods of abnormally low rainfall leading to water scarcity, crop failure, and increased risk of wildfires, with significant health and livelihood consequences.

fields.name: k_extreme-weather-events|2
fields.title: E.2 Climate factors - Extreme weather events - Extreme cold
fields.description: Episodes of abnormally low temperatures, including cold snaps and blizzards, associated with increased risk of hypothermia, cardiovascular events, and respiratory illness.

fields.name: k_extreme-weather-events|3
fields.title: E.2 Climate factors - Extreme weather events - Extreme heat
fields.description: Periods of abnormally high temperatures, including heatwaves, that pose direct health risks such as heat exhaustion, heat stroke, and excess mortality.

fields.name: k_extreme-weather-events|4
fields.title: E.2 Climate factors - Extreme weather events - Floods
fields.description: Temporary inundation of normally dry land caused by excessive rainfall, storm surges, or rapid snowmelt, posing risks to human health, displacement, and infrastructure.

fields.name: k_extreme-weather-events|5
fields.title: E.2 Climate factors - Extreme weather events - Storms
fields.description: Intense meteorological events including tropical cyclones, hurricanes, typhoons, and severe thunderstorms, causing wind damage, flooding, and displacement.

fields.name: k_extreme-weather-events|6
fields.title: E.2 Climate factors - Extreme weather events - Wildfires
fields.description: Uncontrolled fires in natural vegetation, increasingly associated with drought and heat, producing smoke and air pollution with severe respiratory and cardiovascular health impacts.

fields.name: k_climate-forcing-agents|0
fields.title: E.3 Climate factors - Climate forcing agents - (Unspecified) greenhouse gases
fields.description: Atmospheric gases that trap heat and contribute to the greenhouse effect, referred to collectively without specifying the individual gas type.

fields.name: k_climate-forcing-agents|1
fields.title: E.3 Climate factors - Climate forcing agents - Carbon dioxide (CO₂)
fields.description: The primary long-lived greenhouse gas produced by fossil fuel combustion, deforestation, and industrial processes, responsible for the majority of anthropogenic radiative forcing.

fields.name: k_climate-forcing-agents|2
fields.title: E.3 Climate factors - Climate forcing agents - Fluorinated gases / hydrofluorocarbons / perfluorocarbons / sulfur hexafluoride / nitrogen trifluoride
fields.description: A group of potent synthetic greenhouse gases used in industrial applications, refrigeration, and electronics manufacturing, with very high global warming potentials and long atmospheric lifetimes.

fields.name: k_climate-forcing-agents|3
fields.title: E.3 Climate factors - Climate forcing agents - Methane (CH₄)
fields.description: A potent short-lived greenhouse gas emitted from livestock, rice cultivation, landfills, and fossil fuel extraction, with a global warming potential far exceeding that of CO₂ over 20 years.

fields.name: k_climate-forcing-agents|4
fields.title: E.3 Climate factors - Climate forcing agents - Nitrous oxide (N₂O)
fields.description: A greenhouse gas and ozone-depleting substance emitted primarily from agricultural soils, livestock, and nitrogen fertilisers, with a high global warming potential.

fields.name: k_climate-forcing-agents|5
fields.title: E.3 Climate factors - Climate forcing agents - Ozone-depleting substances / chlorofluorocarbons / hydrochlorofluorocarbons / halons / carbon tetrachloride / methyl chloroform
fields.description: Chemical compounds that destroy stratospheric ozone and act as potent greenhouse gases, regulated under the Montreal Protocol due to their combined climate and health impacts.

fields.name: k_climate-forcing-agents|6
fields.title: E.3 Climate factors - Climate forcing agents - Particulate matter (PM10) / fine particulate matter (PM2.5) / black/organic carbon / sulfate/nitrate aerosols
fields.description: Airborne particles of 10 or 2.5 micrometres or less in diameter. Fine particulate matter can include components such as black carbon and sulfate aerosols, that affect both climate and human health through respiratory and cardiovascular pathways.

fields.name: k_climate-forcing-agents|7
fields.title: E.3 Climate factors - Climate forcing agents - Tropospheric ozone (O₃)
fields.description: A short-lived climate pollutant and air quality hazard formed by photochemical reactions between nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds, harmful to respiratory health.

fields.name: k_fossil-fuels|0
fields.title: E.4 Climate factors - Fossil fuels - (Unspecified) fossil fuels
fields.description: Fossil fuel use or combustion where the specific fuel type is not identified, used when studies refer to fossil fuels in general without distinguishing between coal, oil, or gas.

fields.name: k_fossil-fuels|1
fields.title: E.4 Climate factors - Fossil fuels - Coal
fields.description: A solid fossil fuel formed from ancient plant matter, the most carbon-intensive energy source and a major contributor to greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution.

fields.name: k_fossil-fuels|2
fields.title: E.4 Climate factors - Fossil fuels - Natural gas
fields.description: A fossil fuel composed primarily of methane, used for heating, electricity generation, and industrial processes, with lower CO₂ emissions than coal but significant methane leakage risks.

fields.name: k_fossil-fuels|3
fields.title: E.4 Climate factors - Fossil fuels - Oil
fields.description: A liquid fossil fuel refined into petroleum products including petrol, diesel, and jet fuel, a major source of greenhouse gas emissions from transport and industry.

fields.name: k_interventions-measures-responses|0
fields.title: F. Interventions / responses / solutions - Behavior / culture
fields.description: Human behaviours, social practices, and cultural norms that influence greenhouse gas emissions or shape vulnerability and resilience to climate change impacts.

fields.name: k_interventions-measures-responses|1
fields.title: F. Interventions / responses / solutions - Community-based
fields.description: Locally designed and led interventions that mobilise communities to address climate-health risks, drawing on local knowledge, social networks, and collective action.

fields.name: k_interventions-measures-responses|2
fields.title: F. Interventions / responses / solutions - Ecosystem-based
fields.description: Interventions that use the sustainable management, conservation, or restoration of ecosystems to reduce climate-related health risks and deliver co-benefits for biodiversity and human wellbeing, including urban green-blue infrastructure, coastal and marine protection, and forest and land management.

fields.name: k_interventions-measures-responses|3
fields.title: F. Interventions / responses / solutions - Institutional
fields.description: Actions taken by formal organisations and institutions — including governments, health systems, and international bodies — to build climate resilience and coordinate adaptation or mitigation efforts, spanning health system governance, research and education, emergency management, and international development.

fields.name: k_interventions-measures-responses|4
fields.title: F. Interventions / responses / solutions - Policy
fields.description: Formal rules, regulations, and governance instruments designed by governments or international bodies to drive climate mitigation, adaptation, or resilience-building.

fields.name: k_interventions-measures-responses|5
fields.title: F. Interventions / responses / solutions - Technology / infrastructure
fields.description: Physical systems, equipment, and built infrastructure deployed to address environmental, social, or economic challenges, including systems designed to reduce emissions, improve resilience, or support service delivery.

fields.name: dsny000097_sub|0
fields.title: Behavior / culture Category - Adaptation behaviours
fields.description: Deliberate actions taken by individuals or communities to reduce exposure or vulnerability to climate-related hazards and protect health and livelihoods.

fields.name: dsny000097_sub|1
fields.title: Behavior / culture Category - Mitigation behaviours
fields.description: Voluntary or encouraged changes in individual and household behaviour that reduce greenhouse gas emissions across key consumption domains.

fields.name: dsny000098_sub|0
fields.title: Adaptation behaviours Category - Civic engagement
fields.description: Participation in collective and political processes aimed at influencing climate policy, community resilience planning, or social responses to climate hazards.

fields.name: dsny000098_sub|1
fields.title: Adaptation behaviours Category - Household protection
fields.description: Actions taken at the household level to reduce exposure to hazards or improve living conditions, such as installing insulation, flood barriers, ventilation, or emergency preparedness measures.

fields.name: dsny000098_sub|2
fields.title: Adaptation behaviours Category - Learning
fields.description: Acquiring knowledge and skills that enable individuals and communities to understand risks, make informed decisions, and adapt their behaviours and livelihoods accordingly.

fields.name: dsny000098_sub|3
fields.title: Adaptation behaviours Category - Lifestyle change in place
fields.description: Changes to daily routines, work patterns, or living arrangements made within a person's current location in response to changing conditions, without relocating.

fields.name: dsny000098_sub|4
fields.title: Adaptation behaviours Category - Migration
fields.description: Movement of individuals or communities away from areas made uninhabitable or highly hazardous by climate change, including both voluntary relocation and forced displacement.

fields.name: dsny000098_sub|5
fields.title: Adaptation behaviours Category - Other behaviour related to adaptation
fields.description: Adaptation behaviours not classified under the specific categories of civic engagement, psychological coping, household protection, learning, lifestyle change in place, migration, or self-protection.

fields.name: dsny000098_sub|6
fields.title: Adaptation behaviours Category - Psychological coping
fields.description: Psychological strategies and mental health practices that individuals use to manage stress, anxiety, and trauma associated with climate change and climate-related disasters.

fields.name: dsny000098_sub|7
fields.title: Adaptation behaviours Category - Self-protection
fields.description: Individual actions taken to protect personal health from climate hazards, such as using sunscreen, staying hydrated during heat events, or wearing respiratory protection during wildfires.

fields.name: dsny000107_sub|0
fields.title: Mitigation behaviours Category - Behaviour related to food/diet
fields.description: Changes in dietary patterns and food purchasing behaviour, such as reducing meat intake, minimising food waste, or choosing locally produced food, to lower the environmental footprint of food consumption.

fields.name: dsny000107_sub|1
fields.title: Mitigation behaviours Category - Behaviour related to goods/consumption/services
fields.description: Reductions or shifts in the purchase and use of physical goods and services to lower associated environmental impacts, including buying less, repairing, reusing, or choosing lower-impact products and services.

fields.name: dsny000107_sub|2
fields.title: Mitigation behaviours Category - Behaviour related to households
fields.description: Actions taken at the household level to reduce energy consumption and associated emissions, including reducing heating and cooling use, improving insulation, and adopting lower-emission energy sources.

fields.name: dsny000107_sub|3
fields.title: Mitigation behaviours Category - Behaviour related to mobility
fields.description: Behavioural changes in how individuals travel and commute, such as switching to public transport, cycling, walking, or reducing vehicle use, to reduce transport-related emissions.

fields.name: dsny000107_sub|4
fields.title: Mitigation behaviours Category - Other behaviour related to mitigation
fields.description: Mitigation behaviours not classified under the specific categories of mobility, household, food and diet, or goods and consumption.

fields.name: dsny000588_sub|0
fields.title: Community-based Category - Community-based adaptation
fields.description: Locally designed and led responses to climate-health risks, drawing on community knowledge and priorities to develop contextually appropriate adaptation strategies.

fields.name: dsny000588_sub|1
fields.title: Community-based Category - Cultural identity
fields.description: Culturally grounded practices, knowledge systems, and identities that support individual and community wellbeing, including indigenous-led approaches and the preservation of connections to land and heritage.

fields.name: dsny000588_sub|2
fields.title: Community-based Category - Land / resource rights
fields.description: The legal and customary rights of communities and indigenous peoples to access, use, and govern land and natural resources, underpinning livelihood security and self-determination.

fields.name: dsny000588_sub|3
fields.title: Community-based Category - Participatory governance
fields.description: Processes that involve communities in decision-making and planning, ensuring local voices shape policies, programmes, and strategies that affect them.

fields.name: dsny000588_sub|4
fields.title: Community-based Category - Social cohesion / mutual aid
fields.description: Community networks and informal support systems that enable mutual assistance during times of stress or shock, including food sharing, community care, and grassroots first response.

fields.name: dsny000588_sub|5
fields.title: Community-based Category - Z_Other community-based interventions
fields.description: Community-based interventions not classified under community-based adaptation, participatory governance, social cohesion, cultural identity, or land and resource rights.

fields.name: dsny000113_sub|0
fields.title: Ecosystem-based Category - Coastal / marine protection
fields.description: Conservation and restoration of coastal and marine ecosystems including mangroves, coral reefs, and wetlands, providing storm surge protection, food security, flood buffering, and wellbeing co-benefits.

fields.name: dsny000113_sub|1
fields.title: Ecosystem-based Category - Forest / land management
fields.description: Sustainable management and restoration of forests and land, including wildfire prevention, reforestation, agroforestry, peatland restoration for biodiversity and carbon sequestration, regenerative agriculture for soil health and food security, and ecological approaches to reducing disease vector habitat.

fields.name: dsny000113_sub|2
fields.title: Ecosystem-based Category - Urban green-blue infrastructure
fields.description: Parks, street trees, green corridors, and urban water bodies that reduce heat island effects, support mental health, and increase urban resilience through ecosystem services.

fields.name: dsny000113_sub|3
fields.title: Ecosystem-based Category - Z_Other ecosystem-based interventions
fields.description: Ecosystem-based interventions not classified under urban green-blue infrastructure, coastal and marine protection, or forest and land management.

fields.name: dsny000114_sub|0
fields.title: Institutional Category - Emergency / disaster management
fields.description: Systems and institutions for preparedness, response, and recovery in relation to emergencies and disasters, including early warning, evacuation planning, and surge capacity for acute events.

fields.name: dsny000114_sub|1
fields.title: Institutional Category - Health system governance
fields.description: Institutional actions to design and strengthen health systems for climate resilience, including decentralisation, workforce and capacity building in climate-sensitive disease, updating clinical guidelines for climate risks, and ensuring flood, heat, and storm resilience of health facilities and supply chains.

fields.name: dsny000114_sub|2
fields.title: Institutional Category - International development / aid
fields.description: International funding, technical assistance, and development programmes directed at lower-income countries to support economic development, institutional capacity, and service delivery.

fields.name: dsny000114_sub|3
fields.title: Institutional Category - Research / knowledge systems / education
fields.description: Research infrastructure, knowledge translation systems, and educational programmes that build understanding of risks and promote evidence-informed decision-making and behaviour change at individual or community level.

fields.name: dsny000114_sub|4
fields.title: Institutional Category - Z_Other institution-based interventions
fields.description: Institutional interventions not classified under health system governance, research and education, emergency management, or international development and aid.

fields.name: dsny000087_sub|0
fields.title: Policy Category - Fiscal / incentive policy
fields.description: Market-based and fiscal mechanisms such as carbon taxes, emissions trading schemes, and subsidies used to incentivise emissions reductions or climate adaptation investments.

fields.name: dsny000087_sub|1
fields.title: Policy Category - Health-in-all-policies
fields.description: A governance approach that systematically integrates health considerations into climate policy and climate considerations into health policy, recognising that health outcomes are shaped by decisions made across multiple sectors including energy, transport, food, and land use.

fields.name: dsny000087_sub|2
fields.title: Policy Category - International / multilateral agreements
fields.description: Formal binding or non-binding agreements between nations or organisations to coordinate action on climate change, including treaties, protocols, and multilateral accords, e.g. UNFCCC mechanisms, Paris Agreement, WHO frameworks.

fields.name: dsny000087_sub|3
fields.title: Policy Category - National / subnational policy
fields.description: Institutional frameworks, strategies, and targets that guide governments and organisations in planning and implementing climate action, including national determined contributions, national adaptation plans and climate plans (e.g. land use policy, city-level climate health strategies, spatial planning, urban heat island reduction, flood plain management), surveillance and early-warning policy (mandated disease surveillance, heat alert systems), climate-change related public health information and education.

fields.name: dsny000087_sub|4
fields.title: Policy Category - Regulatory / legislative policy
fields.description: Legally binding rules, standards, and enforcement mechanisms that mandate emissions reductions, land use changes, or other climate-related behaviours by governments, industries, or individuals. E.g. emissions standards, environmental health regulations, fossil fuel bans.

fields.name: dsny000093_sub|0
fields.title: Technology / infrastructure Category - Adaptation technologies / infractstructure
fields.description: Technologies and built infrastructure designed to reduce vulnerability to climate impacts, including flood defences, heat-resilient buildings, and early warning systems.

fields.name: dsny000093_sub|1
fields.title: Technology / infrastructure Category - Emitting technologies / infrastructure
fields.description: Technologies and infrastructure that generate significant greenhouse gas emissions, whose phase-out or retrofitting is central to climate mitigation strategies. Covers so-called brown technologies.

fields.name: dsny000093_sub|2
fields.title: Technology / infrastructure Category - Mitigation technologies / infrastructure
fields.description: Technologies and infrastructure designed to reduce or eliminate greenhouse gas emissions.

fields.name: dsny000095_sub|0
fields.title: Adaptation technologies / infractstructure Category - Adaptive built environment
fields.description: Built environment designs and retrofits that reduce heat exposure and improve thermal comfort, including cool roofs, reflective surfaces, passive cooling design, and heat-resilient housing construction.

fields.name: dsny000095_sub|1
fields.title: Adaptation technologies / infractstructure Category - Climate-resilient water / sanitation
fields.description: Water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) infrastructure designed to remain functional under changing precipitation patterns, including flood-proof and drought-resilient water supply systems and sanitation systems adapted to climate variability.

fields.name: dsny000095_sub|2
fields.title: Adaptation technologies / infractstructure Category - Coastal / flood defence
fields.description: Physical infrastructure protecting coastal and flood-prone communities from climate-related inundation, including sea walls, improved drainage systems, and managed retreat programmes that reduce population exposure.

fields.name: dsny000095_sub|3
fields.title: Adaptation technologies / infractstructure Category - Digital / data-based technology / infrastructure
fields.description: Digital tools and data infrastructure supporting climate-health surveillance and response, including remote sensing, climate-health surveillance platforms, vector surveillance systems, and early warning and forecasting systems for climate-sensitive health risks.

fields.name: dsny000095_sub|4
fields.title: Adaptation technologies / infractstructure Category - Food security technology
fields.description: Technologies that maintain food availability and safety under a changing climate, including drought-resistant crop varieties and cold chain systems that preserve food safety under warming conditions.

fields.name: dsny000095_sub|5
fields.title: Adaptation technologies / infractstructure Category - Other adaptation technologies / infrastructure
fields.description: Adaptation technologies and infrastructure not classified under the specific categories of water and sanitation, built environment, digital systems, food security, or coastal and flood defence.

fields.name: dsny000096_sub|0
fields.title: Emitting technologies / infrastructure Category - Carbon-intensive built environment
fields.description: Buildings with poor insulation or energy performance that rely on fossil fuel heating and cooling systems, contributing to both emissions and energy poverty.

fields.name: dsny000096_sub|1
fields.title: Emitting technologies / infrastructure Category - Fossil fuel-based energy systems
fields.description: Power generation infrastructure using coal, oil, or gas combustion, associated with significant greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution health burdens.

fields.name: dsny000096_sub|2
fields.title: Emitting technologies / infrastructure Category - High-emission agricultural infrastructure
fields.description: Agricultural systems with high greenhouse gas footprints, including intensive livestock operations, synthetic fertiliser supply chains, and irrigation systems with large energy demands.

fields.name: dsny000096_sub|3
fields.title: Emitting technologies / infrastructure Category - Industrial / extractive infrastructure
fields.description: Mining, cement, steel, chemical, and other extractive and heavy industrial processes associated with high greenhouse gas emissions and direct health burdens from air, water, and soil pollution.

fields.name: dsny000096_sub|4
fields.title: Emitting technologies / infrastructure Category - Internal combustion transport infrastructure
fields.description: Road networks and vehicle fleets designed around internal combustion engines, generating traffic-related air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions with well-documented health impacts.

fields.name: dsny000096_sub|5
fields.title: Emitting technologies / infrastructure Category - Waste infrastructure with high emissions
fields.description: Waste disposal systems including landfills and open burning that generate methane and toxic air pollutants, contributing to both climate forcing and direct health harm.

fields.name: dsny000096_sub|6
fields.title: Emitting technologies / infrastructure Category - Z_Other emitting technologies / infrastructure
fields.description: Emitting technologies and infrastructure not classified under the specific categories of energy, transport, agriculture, built environment, industrial, or waste systems.

fields.name: dsny000094_sub|0
fields.title: Mitigation technologies / infrastructure Category - Carbon capture
fields.description: Engineered systems that capture CO₂ from point sources or directly from the atmosphere and store it permanently, including carbon capture and storage (CCS) and direct air capture technologies.

fields.name: dsny000094_sub|1
fields.title: Mitigation technologies / infrastructure Category - Clean energy systems
fields.description: Technologies and infrastructure for producing and distributing energy from low- or zero-carbon sources, including renewable energy systems, household energy access, cookstove replacement reducing indoor air pollution and emissions, and smart grid optimisation.

fields.name: dsny000094_sub|2
fields.title: Mitigation technologies / infrastructure Category - Energy-efficiency
fields.description: Technologies and infrastructure that reduce energy consumption, including energy-efficient appliances, green buildings, housing insulation, and retrofits that reduce heating and cooling energy demand.

fields.name: dsny000094_sub|3
fields.title: Mitigation technologies / infrastructure Category - Low-emission transport
fields.description: Infrastructure and systems enabling low-emission travel and transport, including active travel networks, electric vehicle charging infrastructure, and public transit systems.

fields.name: dsny000094_sub|4
fields.title: Mitigation technologies / infrastructure Category - Sustainable food systems
fields.description: Low-emission agricultural technologies and food production systems, including plant-based food production, sustainable land management, and infrastructure for reducing food loss and waste.

fields.name: dsny000094_sub|5
fields.title: Mitigation technologies / infrastructure Category - Waste management / circular economy
fields.description: Sanitation and waste management systems that reduce methane emissions and disease vectors, including circular economy approaches that minimise waste generation and improve resource recovery.

fields.name: dsny000094_sub|6
fields.title: Mitigation technologies / infrastructure Category - Z_Other mitigation technologies / infrastructure
fields.description: Mitigation technologies and infrastructure not classified under the specific categories of clean energy, transport, energy efficiency, food systems, waste management, or carbon capture.

fields.name: k_sectors|0
fields.title: G. Sectors - Agriculture / fishing / forestry (Sector)
fields.description: The sector encompassing crop cultivation, livestock rearing, aquaculture, fishing, and forest management.

fields.name: k_sectors|1
fields.title: G. Sectors - Buildings / housing (Sector)
fields.description: The sector covering residential and commercial buildings, housing provision, and construction.

fields.name: k_sectors|2
fields.title: G. Sectors - Education (Sector)
fields.description: The sector encompassing formal and informal education systems, including schools, universities, and vocational institutions.

fields.name: k_sectors|3
fields.title: G. Sectors - Energy/Extractives (Sector)
fields.description: The sector covering electricity generation, fuel production, and resource extraction, including both fossil fuel and renewable energy systems.

fields.name: k_sectors|4
fields.title: G. Sectors - Finance (Sector)
fields.description: The sector encompassing banking, insurance, investment, and financial services, including public and private finance mechanisms.

fields.name: k_sectors|5
fields.title: G. Sectors - Healthcare (Sector)
fields.description: The sector providing medical care, public health services, and health infrastructure, including hospitals, primary care, and preventive health services.

fields.name: k_sectors|6
fields.title: G. Sectors - Industry / trade / services (Sector)
fields.description: The sector encompassing manufacturing, retail, wholesale trade, and commercial services.

fields.name: k_sectors|7
fields.title: G. Sectors - Information and communications technologies (Sector)
fields.description: The sector covering telecommunications, digital infrastructure, and information technology, including hardware, software, and connectivity systems.

fields.name: k_sectors|8
fields.title: G. Sectors - Military (Sector)
fields.description: The military sector is the part of a country’s economy and government responsible for producing, organizing, and maintaining armed forces and defense capabilities, including personnel, equipment, operations, and infrastrucutre.

fields.name: k_sectors|9
fields.title: G. Sectors - Public administration (Sector)
fields.description: The sector encompassing government agencies, civil services, and public institutions responsible for policy-making, regulation, and the delivery of public services in the context of climate change.

fields.name: k_sectors|10
fields.title: G. Sectors - Social protection (Sector)
fields.description: The sector providing social safety nets, welfare services, and support systems that protect vulnerable populations from economic and social risks.

fields.name: k_sectors|11
fields.title: G. Sectors - Transportation (Sector)
fields.description: The sector covering road, rail, air, and maritime transport systems, including infrastructure, vehicles, and logistics operations.

fields.name: k_sectors|12
fields.title: G. Sectors - Water / sanitation / waste management (Sector)
fields.description: The sector responsible for water supply, sewage treatment, and solid waste management.

fields.name: k_actors|0
fields.title: H. Actors - Civil society (Actor)
fields.description: Non-profit organisations, advocacy groups, and community-based organisations that represent public interests, support communities, and hold governments and businesses accountable.

fields.name: k_actors|1
fields.title: H. Actors - Governments (Actor)
fields.description: National, regional, and local government bodies responsible for setting policy, enacting legislation, and implementing programmes within their jurisdictions.

fields.name: k_actors|2
fields.title: H. Actors - Households / individuals (Actor)
fields.description: Individual people and domestic units whose everyday choices, behaviours, and circumstances make them both agents of and subjects of wider social and environmental change.

fields.name: k_actors|3
fields.title: H. Actors - Private sector (Actor)
fields.description: Commercial enterprises, industries, and business associations whose operations, investments, and innovations shape economic and environmental outcomes.

fields.name: k_actors|4
fields.title: H. Actors - Supranational and international organizations (Actor)
fields.description: Supranational bodies including United Nations agencies, multilateral development banks, and intergovernmental organisations that coordinate policy, financing, and action across nations.

fields.name: k_governance-scale|0
fields.title: I. Governance scale - Global (Governance scale)
fields.description: The highest level of governance, encompassing worldwide institutions, agreements, and processes that operate across all nations.

fields.name: k_governance-scale|1
fields.title: I. Governance scale - International - multi-country (Governance scale)
fields.description: Governance arrangements and interventions involving a defined group of countries acting together across national boundaries, such as bilateral partnerships or plurilateral coalitions, without necessarily sharing a geographic region or formal institutional structure.

fields.name: k_governance-scale|2
fields.title: I. Governance scale - International - regional (Governance scale)
fields.description: Governance operating at a regional geographic scale spanning multiple countries within a formally defined geographic or institutional bloc, such as the European Union or the African Union.

fields.name: k_governance-scale|3
fields.title: I. Governance scale - National (Governance scale)
fields.description: Governance and policy implemented at the level of a single sovereign nation, including national legislation, strategic plans, and government-led programmes.

fields.name: k_governance-scale|4
fields.title: I. Governance scale - Sub-national - local / municipal (Governance scale)
fields.description: Governance at the local or municipal level, including city councils and district authorities responsible for planning, service delivery, and local policy implementation.

fields.name: k_governance-scale|5
fields.title: I. Governance scale - Sub-national - regional (Governance scale)
fields.description: Governance at the level of regions or provinces within a single country, such as states, counties, or devolved administrations with defined policy responsibilities.

fields.name: k_governance-scale|6
fields.title: I. Governance scale - Z_Household / individual (Governance scale)
fields.description: The smallest unit of governance scale, referring to decisions and actions taken by individual people or households.

fields.name: k_human-settlements|0
fields.title: J. Human settlements - Formal urban settlements
fields.description: Planned, officially recognised urban areas with functioning administrative systems, legal land tenure, and access to infrastructure and services, categorised by population size following Revi et al. (2025).

fields.name: k_human-settlements|1
fields.title: J. Human settlements - Informal settlements
fields.description: Residential areas characterised by lack of secure land tenure, inadequate infrastructure, poor access to basic services such as water, sanitation, and healthcare, and overcrowding. This category is intentionally broad, encompassing the diverse forms of unplanned or unauthorised settlement that develop on the periphery of formal cities, without relying on contested administrative labels that vary by country.

fields.name: k_human-settlements|2
fields.title: J. Human settlements - Peri-urban settlements
fields.description: Areas at the urban-rural interface characterised by mixed land use, rapid demographic and physical change, and often partial or transitional access to urban services. The term is used variably across research traditions to describe either the rural-urban fringe of a growing city or areas that are administratively rural but functionally urban.

fields.name: dsny000505_sub|0
fields.title: Formal urban settlements Category - Cities
fields.description: Formal urban settlements with a population of between 100,000 and 1,000,000 inhabitants, with established administrative systems, diverse economies, and relatively comprehensive urban infrastructure.

fields.name: dsny000505_sub|1
fields.title: Formal urban settlements Category - Megacities
fields.description: Formal urban settlements with a population exceeding 10,000,000 inhabitants, presenting unique challenges for governance, infrastructure, environmental management, and health system capacity.

fields.name: dsny000505_sub|2
fields.title: Formal urban settlements Category - Million-cities
fields.description: Formal urban settlements with a population of between 1,000,000 and 10,000,000 inhabitants, characterised by complex governance structures, significant economic output, and high population density.

fields.name: dsny000505_sub|3
fields.title: Formal urban settlements Category - Towns
fields.description: Formal urban settlements with a population of fewer than 100,000 inhabitants, typically characterised by local administrative functions, mixed economies, and partial urban service provision.

fields.name: dsny000511_sub|0
fields.title: Informal settlements Category - Refugee / displaced settlements
fields.description: Settlements established to house populations forcibly displaced by conflict, persecution, or disaster, including formal refugee camps, informal displaced person settlements, and spontaneous settlements in host communities. Distinct from other informal settlements in their governance structures, legal frameworks, humanitarian actors, and policy context, and complementary to concepts of forced displacement and migration by capturing the physical and administrative character of where displaced people live rather than the movement itself.

fields.name: dsny000511_sub|1
fields.title: Informal settlements Category - Slums / favelas
fields.description: Dense informal urban settlements characterised by substandard housing, insecure tenure, limited access to clean water and sanitation, overcrowding, and social marginalisation, known by varied local names including favelas, bidonvilles, katchi abadis, and shanty towns.

fields.name: dsny000511_sub|2
fields.title: Informal settlements Category - Z_Other informal settlements
fields.description: Informal settlements not classified as slums, favelas, or refugee and displaced settlements, including other forms of unplanned or unauthorised housing such as illegal subdivisions, informal extensions of formal areas, and transitional settlements.

fields.name: k_geographic-location|0
fields.title: K. Geographic location [automation planned] - Africa (example)
fields.description: Africa is the world's second-largest continent by area and population, comprising 54 sovereign countries on a single landmass connected to Asia via the Sinai Peninsula, bordered by the Mediterranean Sea, Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, and Red Sea.

fields.name: k_country-income|0
fields.title: L. Country income [automation planned] - High
fields.description: Countries classified by the World Bank as having the highest gross national income per capita, generally with the greatest adaptive capacity but also the highest historical contributions to cumulative emissions.

fields.name: k_country-income|1
fields.title: L. Country income [automation planned] - Low
fields.description: Countries classified by the World Bank as having the lowest gross national income per capita, typically facing the greatest climate vulnerability and least adaptive capacity.

fields.name: k_country-income|2
fields.title: L. Country income [automation planned] - Lower middle
fields.description: Countries classified by the World Bank in the lower-middle income tier, often experiencing rapid development while remaining highly vulnerable to climate-related health and economic impacts.

fields.name: k_country-income|3
fields.title: L. Country income [automation planned] - Upper middle
fields.description: Countries classified by the World Bank in the upper-middle income tier, with growing capacity for climate adaptation and mitigation but still facing significant climate risks.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|0
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Arid / semi-arid
fields.description: Regions characterised by low and variable rainfall, high evapotranspiration, and limited soil moisture, encompassing deserts, steppes, and dry shrublands where water scarcity is a primary constraint.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|1
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Boreal forest / taiga
fields.description: The world's largest terrestrial biome, spanning high-latitude northern regions and characterised by coniferous forest, cold winters, and short growing seasons, playing a major role in global carbon storage.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|2
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Coral reef
fields.description: Shallow marine ecosystems built by calcium carbonate-secreting corals, supporting exceptional biodiversity and coastal protection but highly vulnerable to ocean warming and acidification.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|3
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Delta / floodplain
fields.description: Low-lying landforms formed by sediment deposition at river mouths or along river corridors, characterised by high agricultural productivity and biodiversity but acute vulnerability to flooding, sea-level rise, and storm surge.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|4
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Desert
fields.description: Arid landscapes receiving very low annual precipitation, characterised by sparse vegetation and high temperatures, making them particularly vulnerable to heat stress and water scarcity.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|5
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Farmland
fields.description: Land used for agricultural production including arable crops, pasture, and mixed farming systems, representing a key interface between environmental conditions and food security.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|6
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Forest
fields.description: Land covered predominantly by trees and associated flora, providing critical ecosystem services including carbon sequestration, biodiversity habitat, and water regulation, all threatened by climate change.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|7
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Freshwater
fields.description: Inland water bodies including rivers, lakes, and streams, whose temperature, flow, and quality are sensitive to climate variability with consequences for drinking water and aquatic health.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|8
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Grassland / savanna
fields.description: Open landscapes dominated by grasses and low vegetation, sensitive to changes in precipitation and temperature, and at increased risk of drought and wildfire under climate change. Includes savanna (dominant in sub-Saharan Africa).

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|9
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Island
fields.description: Land masses surrounded by water, particularly small island developing states, which face existential threats from sea level rise, coastal erosion, and increased storm intensity.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|10
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Mangrove
fields.description: Coastal forest ecosystems dominated by salt-tolerant trees growing in intertidal zones of tropical and subtropical coastlines, providing habitat, carbon storage, and protection against storm surge and coastal erosion.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|11
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Mediterranean
fields.description: A climate zone and biome characterised by hot dry summers and mild wet winters, occurring around the Mediterranean Basin and analogous regions, with distinctive shrubland vegetation and high biodiversity.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|12
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Mountain
fields.description: Elevated terrain characterised by steep slopes and cooler temperatures, where glacier retreat, altered precipitation patterns, and biodiversity shifts are prominent climate change impacts.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|13
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Ocean / coastal
fields.description: Areas where land meets the sea, including coastlines, estuaries, and marine environments, highly exposed to sea level rise, storm surges, and ocean warming.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|14
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Peri-urban
fields.description: The transitional zone at the interface between urban and rural areas, characterised by mixed land use, rapid development, and populations that may lack full access to urban services while facing environmental pressures from adjacent cities.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|15
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Polar
fields.description: Cold, high-latitude environments at the Earth's poles, experiencing some of the fastest rates of climate warming globally, with consequences for sea ice, permafrost, and global sea levels.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|16
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Rainforest
fields.description: Dense tropical forests characterised by high biodiversity and rainfall, playing a critical role in global carbon cycling and increasingly threatened by deforestation and drought.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|17
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Riparian
fields.description: The transitional zone between terrestrial and aquatic environments along the banks of rivers, streams, and other watercourses, characterised by distinctive vegetation and sensitivity to flooding and drought.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|18
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Rural
fields.description: Sparsely populated areas outside urban centres, often reliant on agriculture and natural resources, and facing distinct climate risks including drought, flooding, and reduced service access.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|19
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Subtropical
fields.description: Regions located between the tropics and temperate zones, characterised by warm temperatures year-round, variable rainfall, and a mix of humid and dry subtropical climates.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|20
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Temperate
fields.description: Regions with moderate climates experiencing distinct seasons, where climate change is altering seasonal patterns, increasing extreme weather frequency, and affecting biodiversity.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|21
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Tropical
fields.description: Regions near the equator characterised by warm temperatures and high humidity year-round, where climate change is intensifying heat stress, vector-borne disease risk, and extreme rainfall.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|22
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Tundra
fields.description: A treeless biome found at high latitudes and elevations, characterised by permafrost, low vegetation, and extreme cold, with particular sensitivity to warming temperatures and permafrost thaw.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|23
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Urban
fields.description: Densely populated areas characterised by built infrastructure and high human activity, where urban heat island effects and air pollution amplify climate-related health risks.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|24
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Valley
fields.description: Low-lying areas between hills or mountains, often fertile and densely settled, which can be highly exposed to flooding and temperature extremes under climate change.

fields.name: k_geographic-feature|25
fields.title: M. Geographic feature - Wetland / peatland
fields.description: Low-lying ecosystems saturated with water, including marshes, swamps, and peatlands, which serve as important carbon stores and biodiversity habitats, threatened by drainage and climate change.

fields.name: k_health-exposure|0
fields.title: N.1 Health - Exposure - Air quality (Exposure)
fields.description: Exposure to outdoor or indoor air containing pollutants — including particulate matter, ozone, nitrogen dioxide, and wildfire smoke — at concentrations harmful to health.

fields.name: k_health-exposure|1
fields.title: N.1 Health - Exposure - Extreme weather events (Exposure)
fields.description: Acute exposure to extreme meteorological events — including floods, storms, cyclones, droughts, and wildfires — that cause direct physical harm or injury.

fields.name: k_health-exposure|2
fields.title: N.1 Health - Exposure - Food supply and safety (Exposure)
fields.description: Disruptions or changes to the availability, accessibility, and safety of food, including impacts on nutrition, foodborne pathogen risk, and agricultural productivity.

fields.name: k_health-exposure|3
fields.title: N.1 Health - Exposure - Heat stress (Exposure)
fields.description: Physiological strain placed on the body by elevated ambient temperature and humidity, impairing thermoregulation and increasing the risk of heat-related illness.

fields.name: k_health-exposure|4
fields.title: N.1 Health - Exposure - Social factors (Exposure)
